driver.text: Per Reuters, steep declines in U.S. AI and tech shares are testing the rotation into other sectors that had supported the broader indexes, with investors focused on the large financing needed for AI spending and whether returns will justify it. Disappointing results from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel added to the pressure; Intel fell nearly 29% on Friday, and the S&P 500 tech sector fell 6.8% in October, its biggest monthly drop since March 2025. Separately, per Reuters, oil fell more than 4% on Monday (Brent down 4.2% at $108.64 a barrel by 10:20 GMT) on hopes of progress in talks to end the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

morning.label: Morning Brief
morning.timezoneNote: All times shown in ET (America/New_York). Reuters was read through a Lufkin Daily News republication.

driver.text: Per Reuters, at 7:07 AM ET Dow E-minis were down 0.94%, S&P 500 E-minis down 0.19% and Nasdaq 100 E-minis up 0.13%; the Nasdaq-100 closed Monday more than 10% below its record close, confirming a correction. Apple fell 3.9% premarket after warning that rising memory chip costs will pressure its holiday-quarter gross margin. Palantir fell 7.7% despite beating third-quarter expectations and forecasting fourth-quarter revenue above estimates. Nvidia rose 1.4% after four straight losing sessions. Crude rose after an Iranian official said a deal to end the war was far off. U.S. midterm elections are today.
